subareas.name: Data center construction & buildout
subareas.coverage: Project-level tracking of hyperscale/colocation/AI campus buildouts, construction trends, cancelations, delivery timelines.

sources.name: Data Center Knowledge
sources.why: Core trade press for data center construction, campus plans, and the grid/capacity constraints on buildout.

sources.name: DCD (Data Centre Dynamics)
sources.why: Global trade press tracking data center construction, DCIM, and power/grid interconnection news at project level.

sources.name: gentic.news
sources.why: Focused tracker of the AI data center buildroll: announced vs. actually-built gigawatts, capacity realism.

subareas.name: Chip supply & silicon geopolitics
subareas.coverage: TSMC/Samsung/Intel fabs, advanced node economics, export controls (H20, rare earths), semiconductor supply chains.

sources.name: SemiAnalysis
sources.why: The leading independent analysis house for chip/compute capex, NVIDIA/TSMC economics, advanced-node buildout, and the marginal-cost-of-intelligence thesis that anchors this subarea — first-principles on silicon supply and its value chain.

sources.name: Semiconductor Engineering
sources.why: Dedicated chip-industry trade press covering advanced-node economics, packaging, yield, and fab/equipment supply chains that underpin AI silicon — concrete engineering-level signal for this subarea.

sources.name: SemiWiki
sources.why: Chip-industry analysis and commentary on foundry competitive dynamics, advanced-node roadmaps, and semiconductor market structure — a second independent voice distinct from SemiAnalysis.

subareas.name: AI market structure & capital markets
subareas.coverage: Market concentration among hyperscalers/foundries, GPU customers (NVIDIA map), model economics, AI equity/funding flows.

sources.name: The Synthesis
sources.why: Breaks down 'the supply chain of intelligence' — compute ownership, GPU customer economics, model cost basis, and who controls the AI value chain. Gives this subarea a dedicated market-structure source distinct from SemiAnalysis.

subareas.name: Funding, capex & financing cycles
subareas.coverage: Hyperscaler capex guidance, AI infrastructure financing, debt/IPOs, private equity, and credit pipelines.

sources.name: Street Alpha
sources.why: Tracks whether AI capex is real vs. returns slow to arrive — direct take on capital cycle sustainability.

sources.name: Capital & Compute
sources.why: Dedicated to AI data center financing and the $700B buildout — financing structures behind the capex cycle.

sources.name: Tech Cache
sources.why: Follows where AI money goes next — funding and capex allocation across the AI value chain.

subareas.name: Power constraints on compute
subareas.coverage: Grid interconnection, electricity supply bottleneck for datacenters, grid capacity intelligence, electrification load from AI.

sources.name: Grid Capacity Intelligence
sources.why: Dedicated to grid capacity as it constrains datacenter and AI compute deployment — the power-vs-compute bottleneck.

sources.name: Infrastructure Research
sources.why: Covers the 'shadow grid' and interconnection queues behind the AI datacenter buildout.

sources.name: Alex Lanin
sources.why: Argues 'the megawatt is not the asset' — examines what actually drives value when power constrains compute.

subareas.name: Hyperscaler capex tracking
subareas.coverage: Quarterly capex guidance from Microsoft/Google/Amazon/Meta, capex-to-CS timing, and spending shifts.

sources.name: Wheelie Investor
sources.why: Pieces the hyperscaler AI capex announcements (e.g. Google raising capex) into the systemic 'who gets paid' picture.

sources.name: Platformonomics
sources.why: Publishes the quarterly 'Follow the CAPEX' scoreboard tracking hyperscaler (Microsoft/Google/Amazon/Meta) capex and cloud revenue — a dedicated, non-duplicate source for capex guidance tracking and capex-to-CS timing. Replaces the cross-referenced 404K entry removed for duplicate noise.

sources.name: Terrain Labs
sources.why: Publishes a structured AI credit pipeline across industries feeding the datacenter buildout.

sources.name: Dirt to Data
sources.why: Covers AI infrastructure becoming an institutional asset class and the financing of compute buildout.

subareas.coverage: Industry-wide shipment/revenue data for chips and equipment; market data underpinning AI silicon demand.

sources.name: SIA (Semiconductor Industry Association)
sources.why: Authoritative global semiconductor market data and annual factbook — registry for chip revenue/shipment stats.

news_vs_analysis.analysis: SemiAnalysis, 404K Research, Street Alpha, Capital & Compute, Wheelie Investor, Terrain Labs, Dirt to Data, Grid Capacity Intelligence, Infrastructure Research, Alex Lanin, CSIS provide first-principles analysis.

notes: Excluded subscribed/blacklisted domains: blog.eladgil.com and chamathreads.substack.com. Boundaries respected: no consumer-EV, efficiency-gadget, corporate-sustainability-PR, or climate-activism sources (out of scope). Source-type mix covers 7 distinct types: trade press (DCK, DCD), independent blog (gentic.news, Capital & Compute), newsletter (SemiAnalysis, 404K, Street Alpha, Tech Cache, Grid Capacity Intelligence, Infrastructure Research, Lanin, Wheelie, Terrain Labs, Dirt to Data), think tank (CSIS), and data/registry (SIA). Subareas each have >=1 strong source; construction, chips, capex, and power have 2-3 each to match the breadth of a top AI-infrastructure podcast. SIA has no RSS feed, so its crawl_root points to the market-data page for scraping. Confirmed every domain resolves and serves a feed via check_url except semiconductors.org (registry page). Used only the 10-search discovery budget.
